title: Calendar catalog
text: timescales ships curated catalog named calendar designs, ported predecessor timeslices package. Every id can built fresh calendar(id), objects come pre-built calendars dataset: Two equivalent ways get one: Coverage says design relates real year: complete (every instant slice), truncated (stylised year drops instants — d365 Feb 29), representative (slices stand recurring types rather partition timeline — q4_h24 representative day per quarter). Regularity flags designs whose slices differ length within level (m12_md365: February short).
code: knitr::kable(calendar_catalog()) cal <- calendar("m12_h24")     # build on demand cal2 <- calendars$m12_h24      # pre-built package data identical(cal@leaves, cal2@leaves) #> [1] TRUE

title: Calendar catalog
text: Unlike timeslices originals — gave every slice uniform share — catalog calendars weight slices real duration: January 31/365 year, 1/12. makes recast(rule = "sum") conserve weighted_mean weight correctly.
code: m12 <- calendars$m12 data.frame(slice = m12@leaves$slice, share = round(m12@leaves$share, 4))[1:3, ] #>   slice  share #> 1   m01 0.0849 #> 2   m02 0.0767 #> 3   m03 0.0849

title: Calendar catalog
text: designs models start : m12_md* family carries real month/day structure (non-Cartesian — February short), useful data arrives keyed month day--month:
code: calendars$d365_h24    # 8,760 hourly slices, the full-resolution classic #> Calendar: d365_h24  #> Timeframes (2): #>   - YDAY (365) [token: d365, alignment: drop_feb29] #>   - HOUR (24) [token: h24] #> Leaf slices: 8760 #> year_fraction: 1 #> year_start: month=1, day=1 #> utc_offset_minutes: 0 calendars$m12_h24     # 288 slices: representative day per month #> Calendar: m12_h24  #> Timeframes (2): #>   - MONTH (12) [token: m12] #>   - HOUR (24) [token: h24] #> Leaf slices: 288 #> year_fraction: 1 #> year_start: month=1, day=1 #> utc_offset_minutes: 0 calendars$q4_h24      # 96 slices: representative day per quarter #> Calendar: q4_h24  #> Timeframes (2): #>   - QUARTER (4) [token: q4] #>   - HOUR (24) [token: h24] #> Leaf slices: 96 #> year_fraction: 1 #> year_start: month=1, day=1 #> utc_offset_minutes: 0 md <- calendars$m12_md365 nrow(md@leaves) #> [1] 365 head(md@leaves[md@leaves$MONTH == "m02", ], 2) #>    MONTH MDAY       share   slice weight #> 32   m02  d01 0.002739726 m02_d01     24 #> 33   m02  d02 0.002739726 m02_d02     24 tail(md@leaves[md@leaves$MONTH == "m02", ], 1)   # Feb ends at d28 #>    MONTH MDAY       share   slice weight #> 59   m02  d28 0.002739726 m02_d28     24 instant_to_slice(as.Date(c("2021-03-15", "2020-02-29")), md)  # Feb 29 -> NA #> [1] "m03_d15" NA

title: Calendar catalog
text: Three derived timeframes back compact “typical periods” designs — unlike timeslices, fully datetime-convertible: SEASON — meteorological: WIN = Dec–Feb, SPR, SUM, FAL DAYTYPE — WORKDAY (Mon–Fri) / WEEKEND HOURTYPE — NIGHT (h22–h05), PEAK (h17–h20), DAY (rest) mappings defaults, dogma — register token (e.g. different peak window) register_token() build custom calendar .
code: dtm <- as.POSIXct(c("2021-01-15 03:00", "2021-01-16 18:00",                     "2021-07-14 12:00"), tz = "UTC") instant_to_slice(dtm, calendars$s4_hp3) #> [1] "WIN_NIGHT" "WIN_PEAK"  "SUM_DAY" instant_to_slice(dtm, calendars$wk2_h24) #> [1] "WORKDAY_h03" "WEEKEND_h18" "WORKDAY_h12"

title: Calendar catalog
text: autoplot() (plot()) draws calendar’s structure icicle: one band per timeframe ANNUAL root top, rectangle widths equal slice shares, x spanning year [0, 1]. gradient restarts inside parent (color_pattern = "within"), nested structure visible glance:    Dense calendars stay fast — rows beyond max_segments binned drawing:  geometry available without ggplot2 via calendar_layout() — plain data.frame rectangles, usable plotting system: calendar_plot() data--calendar heatmap: hand data.frame keyed slice (nothing, see share structure). layout follows hierarchy — finest timeframe y, next x, coarser levels facets:

title: Concepts
text: timescales built around three concentric ideas. Working centre: Timeframes — atomic vocabulary (YEAR, MONTH, HOUR, …). Tokens — named recipes labels one timeframe (e.g. m12 = m01..m12, m12a = JAN..DEC). Calendars — actual partition year labelled leaves, formed composing tokens. users ever touch layer 3.

title: Concepts
text: timeframe unit time calendar can carry labels. package ships fixed core set: function as_timeframe() extracts value chosen timeframe datetime: format = "token" returns label style built-tokens use, calendar machinery needs internally.
code: CORE_TIMEFRAMES #>  [1] "YEAR"     "QUARTER"  "MONTH"    "MDAY"     "YDAY"     "HOUR"     #>  [7] "MINUTE"   "SECOND"   "WDAY"     "WHOUR"    "MWEEK"    "WEEK"     #> [13] "SEASON"   "DAYTYPE"  "HOURTYPE" t <- as.POSIXct("2025-04-15 13:45", tz = "UTC") as_timeframe(t, "MONTH") #> [1] 4 as_timeframe(t, "MONTH", format = "token") #> [1] "m04" as_timeframe(t, "HOUR") #> [1] 13 as_timeframe(t, "WDAY", format = "token") #> [1] "TUE"

title: Concepts
text: token named, reusable recipe labels one timeframe, plus label’s within-year share. Tokens vocabularies shared across calendars. built-ins: Custom tokens added register_token(), optionally declaring alignment rule (see ).

what: Alignment: mapping real years onto stylised ones
title: Concepts
text: d365 calendar label Feb 29; d360 calendar none last days December. Alignment rules (ALIGNMENT_RULES) declare happens instants: drop_feb29 (Feb 29 NA, later ydays shift Dec 31 still d365), drop_last, repeat_last (clamp last label — week 53 folds w52), exact (error). Built-tokens carry sensible defaults; calendars record meta$alignment, instant_to_slice() accepts override.

title: Concepts
text: Calendar actual product one tokens. leaves resulting tree slices rest model talks . Three constructors, increasing flexibility: first two compose tokens Cartesian product; share product per-token shares scaled year_fraction. third escape hatch irregular calendars (e.g. representative weeks intentionally cover full year).
code: calendar("m12_h24")                    # layer 1: by name calendar_build("m12", "h24")           # layer 2: by token list calendar_from_leaves(leaves, ...)      # layer 3: by raw leaf table

what: What the leaves table looks like
title: Concepts
code: cal <- calendar("q4_h24") head(cal@leaves, 3) #>   QUARTER HOUR      share weight  slice #> 1      Q1  h00 0.01027397     90 Q1_h00 #> 2      Q2  h00 0.01038813     91 Q2_h00 #> 3      Q3  h00 0.01050228     92 Q3_h00 cat(nrow(cal@leaves), "leaves, share sums to", sum(cal@leaves$share)) #> 96 leaves, share sums to 1

title: Concepts
text: Conversion central verb. recast() function handles upsampling, downsampling, irregular--irregular mappings, given calendars cover year fraction.
code: cal_m <- calendar("m12")     # source: monthly cal_q <- calendar("q4")      # target: quarterly  monthly <- data.frame(   slice = cal_m@leaves$slice,   load  = c(120, 118, 105,  92,  85,  88,  95, 100,  98,  90, 105, 122) )  recast(monthly, from = cal_m, to = cal_q, year = 2025,        rule = "weighted_mean", by = "day") #>   slice      load #> 1    Q1 114.21111 #> 2    Q2  88.29670 #> 3    Q3  97.66304 #> 4    Q4 105.67391

title: Concepts
text: Conversion routes base grid real instants: source values projected instants, aggregated target slices, aggregation disaggregation one operation (RECAST_RULES): weighted_mean mean differ exactly calendar’s declared shares differ real-time coverage. Per-parameter defaults can registered register_rule(), pairwise calendar--calendar override register_conversion(). Instants covered one calendars governed na_action = "drop" (warns), "error", "keep" (explicit NA row conserves totals).

what: Within-calendar aggregation and the ANNUAL root
title: Concepts
text: Every calendar implicit whole-year root named ANNUAL. calendar_at_level() truncates calendar one timeframes, recast() accepts timeframe name =:
code: cal <- calendar("q4_h24") x <- data.frame(slice = cal@leaves$slice, energy = 1) recast(x, cal, to = "ANNUAL", year = 2025, rule = "sum") #>    slice energy #> 1 ANNUAL     96

title: Concepts
text: Year-bounded calendars, multi-year base. calendar describes one model year (fraction one); base instant grid (base_calendar()) spans real multi-year time, leap years stay representable. Multi-year horizons remain future layer. Label-stable. calendar’s slice IDs ordering fixed construction time. Conversions never mutate . Explicit registries . Constructors return values; token, rule, conversion registries change behaviour register .

title: Data structures
text: Tokens live internal environment, populated load time built-set extensible run time register_token(). token list two required fields one optional: timeframe — one CORE_TIMEFRAMES, expand — zero-argument function returning data.frame(label, share) share summing 1, alignment (optional) — one ALIGNMENT_RULES, inherited calendars built token. Custom tokens behave identically built-ins:
code: list_tokens() #>  [1] "d360"  "d364"  "d365"  "d366"  "h168"  "h24"   "hp3"   "m12"   "m12a"  #> [10] "min60" "q4"    "s4"    "w52"   "w53"   "wd7"   "wk2" m12 <- get_token("m12") m12$timeframe #> [1] "MONTH" head(m12$expand()) #>   label      share #> 1   m01 0.08493151 #> 2   m02 0.07671233 #> 3   m03 0.08493151 #> 4   m04 0.08219178 #> 5   m05 0.08493151 #> 6   m06 0.08219178 register_token("d4q", "YDAY", function() {   data.frame(label = c("Q1d", "Q2d", "Q3d", "Q4d"),              share = c(90, 91, 92, 92) / 365) }) calendar_build("d4q", "h24") #> Calendar: d4q_h24  #> Timeframes (2): #>   - YDAY (4) [token: d4q] #>   - HOUR (24) [token: h24] #> Leaf slices: 96 #> year_fraction: 1 #> year_start: month=1, day=1 #> utc_offset_minutes: 0

title: Data structures
text: validator Calendar enforces: required columns present @leaves, slice unique non-empty, share > 0 sum(share) == meta$year_fraction, weight >= 0, year_start carries valid month (1..12) day (1..31), utc_offset_minutes integer scalar, levels[[tf]] set-equal unique(leaves[[tf]]). violation throws construction time, Calendar hold always internally consistent.

title: Data structures
text: recast() returns data.frame column layout input — slice plus value columns — target calendar’s slice IDs. instant_to_slice() inverse direction (datetime → slice ID) returns character vector length input, NA instants outside calendar’s coverage.
code: src <- data.frame(slice = sprintf("m%02d", 1:12),                   load  = seq(100, 210, length.out = 12)) recast(src, from = calendar("m12"), to = calendar("q4"),        year = 2025, rule = "weighted_mean", by = "day") #>   slice     load #> 1    Q1 110.0000 #> 2    Q2 140.0000 #> 3    Q3 169.8913 #> 4    Q4 200.0000

title: Getting started with timescales
text: Energy-system, climate, operations models carve year discrete time slices. Different models pick different slicings: 365 days, 12 months, 4 quarters × 24 hours, 168 hours representative week, . slice labels arbitrary, shares year model-defined, converting data slicings error-prone. timescales represents slicing Calendar: ordered hierarchy timeframes (YEAR, MONTH, HOUR, …) whose terminal leaves form slices. one object get: stable schema slice labels year-share weights, well-defined mappings real datetimes, well-defined conversions two calendars covering year fraction.

title: Getting started with timescales
text: fastest path uses token-based names: Equivalent declarative form: full control lowest-level constructor calendar_from_leaves(), supply leaves table directly.
code: cal_my <- calendar("m12_h24")    # 12 months × 24 hours = 288 leaves cal_my #> Calendar: m12_h24  #> Timeframes (2): #>   - MONTH (12) [token: m12] #>   - HOUR (24) [token: h24] #> Leaf slices: 288 #> year_fraction: 1 #> year_start: month=1, day=1 #> utc_offset_minutes: 0 cal_my2 <- calendar_build("m12", "h24") identical(cal_my@timeframes, cal_my2@timeframes) #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with timescales
text: Calendar four parts: leaves plain data.frame. row one slice, columns: slice — unique slice ID, share — fraction year, weight — slice weight hours (default share * 8760), one column per timeframe — label level.
code: cal_my@timeframes               # the timeframe hierarchy, coarsest first #> [1] "MONTH" "HOUR" head(cal_my@leaves, 4)          # the leaf table (one row per slice) #>   MONTH HOUR       share weight   slice #> 1   m01  h00 0.003538813     31 m01_h00 #> 2   m02  h00 0.003196347     28 m02_h00 #> 3   m03  h00 0.003538813     31 m03_h00 #> 4   m04  h00 0.003424658     30 m04_h00 cal_my@levels$MONTH             # ordered label vocabulary per timeframe #>  [1] "m01" "m02" "m03" "m04" "m05" "m06" "m07" "m08" "m09" "m10" "m11" "m12" cal_my@meta[c("name", "year_fraction")] #> $name #> [1] "m12_h24" #>  #> $year_fraction #> [1] 1

title: Supported alignment rules — ALIGNMENT_RULES

Fill chronological order (gradient recycling within parent, global), share, weight; auto white/dark labels; rows denser max_segments (default 2000) binned hourly calendars render instantly. calendar_plot() — single data--calendar heatmap: data keyed slice, layout finest--y / next--x / coarser--facets, aggregation fun= timeframes dropped; data plots share structure. Naming convention settled: class-word prefixes (calendar_* now, horizon_* Horizon lands); generics stay bare. Custom stat_*/geom_* layers deferred wrap helpers.

title: timescales (development version)
text: curated calendar library returns, ported timeslices (37 designs) — correctness upgrade: catalog calendars carry duration-proportional shares (January 31/365 year), timeslices originals shipped uniform shares (1/12) contradiction documentation. calendar_catalog() — discoverable table built-designs (id, tokens, timeframes, slice count, coverage, regularity). calendars dataset — 37 pre-built lean package data (~40 KB vs timeslices’ 1.9 MB). calendar(id) now consults catalog first: catalog builds carry meta$coverage / meta$regularity, non-Cartesian m12_md* family (ragged month/day grids — February short) routes dedicated builder. Feb 29 m12_md365 day 31 m12_md360 map NA naturally. New timeframes SEASON (meteorological, WIN = Dec–Feb), DAYTYPE (WORKDAY/WEEKEND), HOURTYPE (DAY/NIGHT h22–h05/PEAK h17–h20) join CORE_TIMEFRAMES full datetime extraction — 9 type-axis designs (s4*, wk2*, hp3, *_hp3) datetime-convertible first time (timeslices construct never populate ). New tokens s4, wk2, hp3 duration-weighted shares.

title: timescales (development version)
text: Fixes five conversion defects diagnosed dev/review-core-plan.md; design decisions recorded dev/review-core.md. recast() now routes every conversion -> base -> B multi-year grid real instants (geoscales atom pattern), projecting source values instants aggregating target slices.

title: timescales (development version)
text: recast(rule = "sum") now conserves totals — source value split across slice’s grid instants summing. Previously values broadcast every instant added (96 unit leaves recast q4_h24 -> q4 returned 8760; now returns 96). recast(rule = "weighted_mean") now weights declared leaves$share. differs "mean" (plain time-weighted grid mean) exactly declared shares differ real-time coverage. expand_calendar() gains year column output (datetime, year, slice) accepts vector years. h168 token now lives new WHOUR timeframe (hour week, Monday-first ISO, h000..h167) instead mis-declared HOUR, maps datetimes correctly. Uncovered grid instants longer dropped silently: recast(na_action = c("drop", "error", "keep")) — "drop" warns, "keep" retains explicit NA slice row totals conserve.

title: timescales (development version)
text: Base calendar: base_calendar(years, , tz) enumerates cached multi-year grid real POSIXct instants — 1:1 correspondence calendars date-time (leap years included: 2020 8784 hourly rows). ANNUAL root within-calendar aggregation: calendar_at_level(cal, tf) truncates calendar one timeframes ("ANNUAL" returns implicit one-slice whole-year root), recast() accepts timeframe name =. Alignment rules (ALIGNMENT_RULES): exact, drop_last, drop_feb29, repeat_last declare real instants beyond calendar’s vocabulary map onto . Stored per-timeframe meta$alignment, seeded tokens (d365 -> drop_feb29, d360/d364 -> drop_last, w52 -> repeat_last), overridable instant_to_slice(). register_token() gains alignment argument. New rules: "copy" (common value, error non-constant) "sd" join RECAST_RULES. Registries (mirroring geoscales): register_rule() / get_rule() / list_rules() / clear_rules() map value-column names default rules; register_conversion() / get_conversion() / list_conversions() / clear_conversions() register pairwise calendar--calendar overrides consulted base route. Vocabulary unification: instant_to_slice() resolves labels formatted-token match first, positional fallback full-cardinality enum vocabularies — m12a (JAN..DEC) custom enum tokens now map instead returning NA. meta$year_start meta$utc_offset_minutes live: model year spans [anchor(y), anchor(y+1)), YDAY/YEAR anchored year_start, local time = UTC + offset throughout instant_to_slice() expand_calendar(). Token provenance restored: calendar_build() records meta$tokens (token per timeframe).

title: timescales 0.1.0.9000
